classification.difficultyReason: The supplied bearing angle and part (a) scaffold the ground-distance calculation; transfer the resulting height to a second vertical triangle.

content.prompt: A tree $BT$ is due north of an observer at $P$ and due west of an observer at $Q$. The two observers are 50 m apart and the bearing of $Q$ from $P$ is $36^\circ$. The angle of elevation of $T$ from $Q$ is $28^\circ$.

spec.description: Ground triangle PBQ and vertical BT, with solid sight lines and PQ, dashed PB, BQ and BT, perpendicular marks at B and light blue angle sectors.
spec.mathematics: PB is north–south and BQ east–west. PQ is 50 m, angle BPQ is 36 degrees and angle BQT is 28 degrees. BT is h.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Hence find the height $h$ of the tree, correct to the nearest metre.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Find the angle of elevation of $T$ from $P$, correct to the nearest degree.

answer.worked:
Let $\alpha$ be the angle of elevation from $P$.

$$\begin{aligned}BP&=50\cos36^\circ\\\tan\alpha&=\frac{h}{BP}\\\alpha&=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{50\sin36^\circ\tan28^\circ}{50\cos36^\circ}\right)\\\alpha&\approx21^\circ\end{aligned}$$
